_comment: Diet engine quality baseline, re-recorded after Phases A-E (76-recipe library, 136-food catalogue). chosen_ingredient_share: the earlier 0.379 was measured while the recipe path was dead for any client who had chosen foods (a loop variable shadowed the similarity index; the planner failed open to templates), so it graded template-only plates. preference_satisfaction (D1) is the recall side: of the foods the chooser picked for a slot, the share that reached that slot's plate at least once in the week. Phase C made variety a week-level objective: a dish's sampling weight falls with its servings in the last seven days, and a dish already served WEEK_MAX_SERVINGS (2) times loses the judge to any fitting built plate. That cap is why distinct_dishes moved 81 -> 79 and dish_rate 0.839 -> 0.774: at a 1,133 kcal breakfast one dish reaches the target and was served six days of seven; those days are now built plates. Measured caps 3 and 4 give dish 0.792 / 0.815 with worst repeats 3 / 4. The gate asserts these as bounds in the direction of improvement. Re-recorded after the independent review: the harness now plans from a fixed date (the seed used to include today's date), dishes are counted by recipe identity rather than by name (substitution suffixes had inflated distinct_dishes), the template solver and the judge use the engine's one rule (inside tolerance first), the judge scores the served plate, augmentation can reach dishes the reach filter used to discard, and the library holds 105 dishes (23 for the ends of the calorie range, 6 protein-dense light dinners). max_repeats_per_client_week is 4, not 2, because the judge no longer serves an off-target plate to avoid a repeat (a reviewer's finding): a 1,200 kcal client's snack carries the day's protein residual, and only one snack dish fits it on three days. That is the library at the end of the calorie range, listed under after-launch, not the sampler: a dish at the cap is never sampled while another fitting dish exists. chosen_ingredient_share falls 0.325 -> 0.290 and preference_satisfaction 0.750 -> 0.688 deliberately: a substitution may no longer replace the ingredient a dish is named after, nor swap one qualifier of a food for another. 'Lentil Soup with Greens (Chickpeas instead of Lentils)' had been counted as a chosen food reaching a dish; it is a different dish wearing the name, and no client would accept it. Dish rate rises 0.833 -> 0.845 in the same measurement. Re-recorded after the fresh-dive engine batch. Most metrics improved: dish rate 0.845 -> 0.857, worst weekly repeat 4 -> 3, chosen share 0.290 -> 0.293, preference satisfaction 0.688 -> 0.750. Two moved the other way and are accepted with reasons. distinct_dishes 61 -> 58: substitution now refuses to swap in a food the client has since disliked or that their allergens forbid, because the dish was then rejected wholesale and the library silently shrank — fewer substitutions, but every one of them servable. twin_identical_meals 0 -> 1: one LIBRARY DISH is the best fit for a slot both before and after the client chooses, which is not a personalisation failure; twin_identical_built stays 0, so every meal the engine builds still changes. The vegetable and fruit slots also have a real density now: they had no entry, scored zero, and fell through to a name tie-break that sorts descending, so the shortlist was the reverse-alphabetical head of the catalogue. Re-recorded after the whole-app fresh dive. The namesake rule now matches plurals and multi-word food names, so 'Lentil Soup (Chickpeas instead of Lentils)' can no longer be served; it reads the English column, so the rule is no longer silently off for Arabic requests. dish_rate 0.857 -> 0.875, distinct_dishes 58 -> 66, twins 1 -> 0. chosen_ingredient_share and preference_satisfaction fall a little: that is the honest cost of refusing substitutions that destroy the dish. min_distinct_portions_per_food is now measured over engine-BUILT plates only — a recipe author's pinned clove of garlic is meant to be identical every time, and counting it made the metric unmeasurable, which is why its bound had to sit at its own floor.
